Lauren / team — see below a concise transfer-impact paragraph and notes for the DPA redline. I recommend we accept most of NovaPay’s edits but propose the language in bold for the Transfer Impact clause.

Transfer Impact paragraph (proposed):
"Redwood has implemented organizational, technical, and contractual safeguards designed to provide an equivalent level of protection to EU/UK personal data when transferred outside the European Economic Area and the UK. These measures include (i) execution of the European Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and the UK International Data Transfer Addendum (IDTA) where applicable, (ii) the use of strong encryption in transit and at rest, (iii) documented access controls and minimization for live customer data, and (iv) independent SOC 2 / ISO 27001 attestations for critical systems. In circumstances where the legal framework of the recipient country could materially affect data protection, Redwood will undertake a targeted Transfer Impact Assessment and implement additional technical or contractual restrictions appropriate to the legal risk."

Notes:
- SCCs + UK IDTA: OK to execute both. We should attach the SCC Annex (we keep a canonical PDF).
- Subprocessor notice: 30 days is fine; offer an expedited review/certification path (technical questionnaire + security attestation) for priority subprocessors.
- Attachments to include with DPA: SCCs_template-Annex.pdf and a brief transfer-impact-summary-2026-04-05.pdf (one page) that explains routing, encryption, and contractual commitments.

Priyom — confirm whether NovaPay requires electronic signature only (DocuSign) or countersignature via AdobeSign (they flagged both). I can approve the DocuSign envelope content once we incorporate Amara’s minor redlines.

Rishi
Head of Privacy, Redwood Inference
